supporting_observations.claim: The alerted host made repeated HTTPS CONNECT requests to updates.pixelforge-suite.com during the alert window, including at 13:37:50, 13:47:45, 13:53:13, 13:58:15, 14:02:29, and 14:07:46 UTC. One intervening attempt at 13:42:31 received proxy status 407.

Endpoint network events attribute the repeated connections to C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe running as leo.martins and connecting to the explicit proxy; for example, records around 13:47:45, 13:53:13, and 14:07:46 show the process and proxy connection.

The observed process, destination, and roughly five-minute checking pattern match the inventory's approved PixelForge updater and its documented update-check interval. The alert’s HTTPS activity is therefore specifically explained by an approved tool rather than merely appearing benign because other evidence is absent.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnels and byte counts, not the HTTPS payload or the contents of the updater’s exchanges.
The supplied records do not include a hash or signature-validation result for pfupdater.exe.
The 13:42:31 CONNECT attempt was recorded as status 407 (authentication required), so that attempt did not establish a successful tunnel.
claims_not_established: The contents of the successful HTTPS sessions or the exact update data exchanged are not established.
The evidence does not independently verify the integrity or signature of the pfupdater.exe binary.
unrelated_findings: DropboxUpdate.exe ran briefly as SYSTEM on WS-LMARTINS-01. Dropbox is not among the approved services; the supplied records do not establish Dropbox file-sharing activity or a corresponding outbound connection. Track separately. (T046-00119, T046-00120, T046-00127, T046-00128)

A credential validation and network logon for sam.okafor on WS-SOKAFOR-01 identify WS-LMARTINS-01 as the source, despite the stated practice that remote administration is performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01. This is outside the alerted HTTPS activity and merits separate review. (T046-00023, T046-00024)

FILE-NWD-01 made an RPC connection to WS-LMARTINS-01 on port 135. The supplied records do not establish its purpose or link it to the alerted HTTPS activity. (T046-00063, T046-00067, T046-00068, T046-00069)
